title: Sense and Sensitivity: Benchmarking LLM Clinical Triage Recommendations with Physician Experts
abstract: arXiv:2609.38600v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in clinical settings, it is critical to evaluate their reliability under realistic variation in clinical text. We study this question in clinical triage, comparing LLMs to practicing physicians under text perturbations that preserve the underlying clinical setting. We introduce a benchmark of over 6,000 clinical scenarios, 7,000 physician annotations, and 225,000 model responses. Using this benchmark, we make two key observations. First, LLMs are more likely than physicians to recommend unnecessary care at baseline, and this tendency increases under perturbed inputs. Further, we find that LLM recommendations are more sensitive to gender and tone perturbations than human recommendations. Together, these results demonstrate that LLMs can vary under clinically irrelevant textual changes, highlighting the need for deployment-oriented evaluations grounded in expert physician behavior.

translated_title: 理智与敏感：以医师专家为基准评估大语言模型的临床分诊建议
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLM）在临床环境中的使用日益增多，评估其在临床文本现实变化下的可靠性至关重要。我们在临床分诊场景中研究这一问题，在保持底层临床情境不变的文本扰动条件下，将大语言模型与执业医师进行比较。我们推出了一个基准数据集，包含超过6,000个临床场景、7,000条医师标注和225,000个模型响应。利用该基准，我们得出两项关键观察结果：首先，在基线条件下，大语言模型比医师更有可能建议不必要的医疗措施，且这种倾向在输入受到扰动后会进一步增加；此外，我们发现大语言模型的建议比人类医师的建议对性别和语气扰动更为敏感。综上，这些结果表明大语言模型的输出可能因临床上无关的文本变化而波动，凸显了以专家医师行为为基础、面向部署的评估的必要性。
tldr: 该研究构建了包含6,000余个临床场景的大规模临床分诊基准，发现大语言模型比执业医师更常建议不必要的医疗措施，且其建议对临床上无关的性别、语气等文本变化更为敏感，凸显了基于专家医师行为开展面向部署评估的必要性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a large-scale clinical triage benchmark with over 6,000 clinical scenarios, showing that LLMs recommend unnecessary care more often than physicians and that their recommendations are more sensitive than human ones to clinically irrelevant gender and tone perturbations in clinical text.
